elements.title: Observation of relativistic bond weakening in seaborgium hexacarbonyl (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Observation of relativistic bond weakening in seaborgium hexacarbonyl

Gas chromatography analysis of compounds formed by the superheavy element seaborgium shows that the hexacarbonyl complex Sg(CO)6 exhibits lower first bond dissociation energy than the lighter chemical homologue W(CO)6, owing to relativistic bond weakening effects.

  • Alexander Yakushev
  • Jadambaa Khuyagbaatar
  • Peter Wieczorek
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: RNA catalysis emerges from dynamic structural ensembles (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
RNA catalysis emerges from dynamic structural ensembles

RNase P RNA forms shifting active and inactive conformers whose catalytic activity depends on Mg2+-driven tertiary-interaction dynamics, which are modulated by binding of accessory proteins.

  • Maximilia F. S. Degenhardt
  • Hermann F. Degenhardt
  • Yun-Xing Wang
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: A thorium-229 optical nuclear clock with feedback loop (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A thorium-229 optical nuclear clock with feedback loop

A thorium-229 nuclear clock is realized by stabilizing a continuous-wave laser to the 148-nm nuclear excitation with a rapid feedback loop based on absorption spectroscopy.

  • L. Toscani De Col
  • T. Riebner
  • T. Schumm
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: Structural basis for regulating lipopolysaccharide transmembrane transport (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Structural basis for regulating lipopolysaccharide transmembrane transport

Structures of the protein machinery in Gram-negative bacteria that transports lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from the cytoplasmic membrane to the outer leaflet of the outer membrane reveal how conformational changes in response to the presence of LPS promote its transport.

  • Rebecca J. Taylor
  • Karanbir S. Pahil
  • Daniel Kahne
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: A nuclear clock synchronized to 229Th (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A nuclear clock synchronized to 229Th

A nuclear clock synchronized to 229Th establishes laser-addressed nuclei as operational clock references and 229Th:CaF2 as a stable, reproducible solid-state platform for compact nuclear clocks and nuclear quantum sensors.

  • Beichen Huang
  • Gaowei Yan
  • Shiqian Ding
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: Hydrogen bonding in water under extreme confinement (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Hydrogen bonding in water under extreme confinement

A new technique allows direct nanoscale observations of the vibrational response of water confined inside carbon nanotubes, revealing that high degrees of confinement disrupt the hydrogen bond network through a fluctuating and highly-dispersed molecular state.

  • Xintong Xu
  • Matthias Kuehne
  • Arun Majumdar
Article07 Oct 2026

elements.title: Alveolar stem cells transdifferentiate to drive bronchiolar regeneration (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Alveolar stem cells transdifferentiate to drive bronchiolar regeneration

Identification of a cross-compartmental cellular mechanism for bronchiolar epithelial repair informs therapeutic strategies for airway injury.

  • Kuo Liu
  • Zixin Liu
  • Bin Zhou
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: Experimental observation of critical topology (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Experimental observation of critical topology

Experimental evidence indicating that critical gapless topological states can be characterized by the entanglement spectrum and wavefunctions is presented, demonstrating persistence of topology at phase boundaries and extension to higher-dimensional systems.

  • Zhi-Kang Lin
  • Li-Wei Wang
  • Jian-Hua Jiang
Article07 Oct 2026

elements.title: Prehistoric global migration of vanishing gut microbes with humans (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Prehistoric global migration of vanishing gut microbes with humans

Microbial species disappearing from industrialized populations have evolved with humans over millennia and migrated worldwide with them—this may have consequences for human health.

  • Matthew M. Carter
  • Zhiru Liu
  • Justin L. Sonnenburg
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: A preinvasive regulatory T cell axis for lung cancer interception (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A preinvasive regulatory T cell axis for lung cancer interception

An effector regulatory T cell circuit is identified that can be monitored in blood samples to track the development of lung cancer, and blockade of this immune network in the preinvasive setting can intercept tumorigenesis to reduce tumour incidence and size.

  • Samuel Gamble
  • Zoe E. Whiteman
  • James L. Reading
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: Mechanism of spliceosome termination (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Mechanism of spliceosome termination

A coordinated sequence of RNA helicases and associated factors dismantles normal and defective spliceosome complexes to enable intron degradation and ensure accurate gene expression.

  • Vytaute Boreikaite
  • Rupert Faraway
  • Clemens Plaschka
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: A 7-eV bandgap semiconductor based on silicon-doped α-(AlxGa1−x)2O3 (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A 7-eV bandgap semiconductor based on silicon-doped α-(AlxGa1−x)2O3

Suboxide molecular-beam epitaxy is used to grow silicon-doped α-(AlxGa1−x)2O3 films with bandgaps exceeding 7.0 eV, enabling the fabrication of a Schottky diode and a field-effect transistor with colossal-bandgap channels.

  • Jacob Steele
  • Debaditya Bhattacharya
  • Darrell. G. Schlom
Article07 Oct 2026

elements.title: tRNA dosage regulates lineage dependency and resistance in prostate cancer (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
tRNA dosage regulates lineage dependency and resistance in prostate cancer

A tRNA-specific regulatory pathway is associated with codon biology, lineage transitions and therapy resistance in prostate cancer.

  • Yeon Soo Kim
  • Sonali Arora
  • Andrew C. Hsieh
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: A chiral superlattice route to spin-split topological antiferromagnetism (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A chiral superlattice route to spin-split topological antiferromagnetism

A chiral superlattice in collinear antiferromagnetic UOTe generates large Berry curvature and spin-polarized currents, enabling anomalous Hall effects and advancing chiral quantum materials for spintronics.

  • Thao Dinh
  • Mengke Liu
  • Su-Yang Xu
Article07 Oct 2026

elements.title: Dynamics of human cardiogenesis and its disruption in trisomy 21 (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Dynamics of human cardiogenesis and its disruption in trisomy 21

Single-cell and spatial multiomics are combined to define niches in the developing human heart, revealing pacemaker-cell organization, cardiomyocyte maturation and compaction, and developmental perturbations associated with trisomy 21.

  • James Cranley
  • Kazumasa Kanemaru
  • Sarah A. Teichmann
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: Australia’s current wildfire crisis linked to colonial land-use change (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Australia’s current wildfire crisis linked to colonial land-use change

A 1,000-year lake-sediment record from southeastern Australia shows that colonial disruption of Indigenous cultural burning transformed open woodland into dense, flammable forest, priming the landscape for today’s climate-driven wildfires.

  • Michael-Shawn Fletcher
  • Anthony Romano
  • Russell Mullett
Article07 Oct 2026

elements.title: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes

Byteification is a general method for retrofitting large language models to operate over bytes such that they approach the capabilities of subword-based systems and may be better for scientific data.

  • Benjamin Minixhofer
  • Tyler Murray
  • Valentin Hofmann
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: Spatially deterministic nucleation of 2D semiconductors by etching flux (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Spatially deterministic nucleation of 2D semiconductors by etching flux

Etching-flux-mediated single-centred nucleation of two-dimensional semiconductors is used to deterministically localize a single nucleation event, expanding semiconductor deposition from controlling where materials grow to controlling where and how crystals can begin to form.

  • Jeongwon Park
  • Jiyun Kim
  • Kibum Kang
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: A split attractor design for rapidly writing a navigational goal (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A split attractor design for rapidly writing a navigational goal

The recurrent h∆K–PFG neural circuit generates persistent heading memories through slow excitation, fast inhibition and a disinhibitory gate, where disinhibition controls the functional coupling of the network to rapidly transition between measurement and memory.

  • Aaron J. Lanz
  • Nicholas D. Kathman
  • Katherine I. Nagel
ArticleOpen Access07 Oct 2026

elements.title: Cryo-EM structure of a methanogen nitrogenase–PII protein supercomplex (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Cryo-EM structure of a methanogen nitrogenase–PII protein supercomplex

Cryo-electron microscopy of a nitrogenase supercomplex from a methane-producing archaeon reveals a mechanism in which PII proteins drive assembly of such structures to regulate nitrogenase activity in response to nitrogen availability.

  • Rajnandani Kashyap
  • Thomas M. Deere
  • Edwin Antony
Article07 Oct 2026
